setup_wizard.title: Quick Hackathon Setup
setup_wizard.description: Answer a few questions and the system will generate a sensible default for sessions, submission fields, and scoring criteria. You can fine-tune everything afterward.
setup_wizard.apply_hint: The wizard replaces the current submission form and scoring criteria with a fresh default. If the hackathon has zero or one session, it also fills in the default round structure.
setup_wizard.format_desc: Define only the round structure here. Region, class, and category stay as optional form fields and filters.

single_round.title: Single Round
single_round.desc: Best for smaller events that go straight into one judging round.

prelim_final.title: Preliminary + Final
prelim_final.desc: The most flexible default: screen projects first, then run a final round.

three_stage.title: Preliminary + Semi + Final
three_stage.desc: Useful for larger events with multiple promotion steps.

setup_wizard.session_generation_note: The current hackathon has little or no round structure yet, so the wizard will generate the default sessions for you.
setup_wizard.session_preserve_note: Multiple sessions already exist. To avoid overwriting live structure, the wizard will leave sessions untouched. Edit them manually in the Sessions tab if needed.
setup_wizard.dimensions_desc: These fields appear in the submission form and become reusable filters in project views, assignment management, and reports.

region.title: Region
region.desc: Useful for city stops, regional tracks, or hybrid online/offline events.

class_name.title: Class
class_name.desc: Useful for courses, bootcamps, departments, or internal cohorts.

category.title: Category
category.desc: Useful for tracks, themes, business lines, or project types.

setup_wizard.submission_desc: Choose how much project detail participants should provide by default.

lean.title: Lean
lean.desc: Keep only the project name and links for the fastest launch.

standard.title: Standard
standard.desc: Balanced and easy to use. Best default for most hackathons.

detailed.title: Detailed
detailed.desc: Require a fuller project write-up for more complex evaluation.

setup_wizard.preview_desc: This is the starting structure. You can keep editing it below after applying.
setup_wizard.no_dimensions: No extra filter dimensions selected yet. You can add them later if needed.

assignments.title: Project Assignments
assignments.subtitle: Assign projects to judges for evaluation
assignments.help: Check the boxes to assign projects to judges. Each project can be assigned to multiple judges.
assignments.auto_desc: Designed for larger events. Filter down to the current project scope first, then pick judges and fill the current session's missing review tasks without overwriting existing assignments.
assignments.judges_per_project_desc: Used by balanced random assignment only. The system spreads new tasks across the selected judges as evenly as possible.
assignments.filters_desc: Use submission fields marked as filterable to narrow the current project scope. All batch actions apply only to the filtered result.
assignments.search_projects_placeholder: Search by title, summary, submitter, or tags
assignments.projects_desc: Select projects to assign to judges
assignments.judges_desc: View judge assignments and assign all projects
assignments.bulk_created: Created {{count}} assignments for the selected judges
assignments.random_created: Created {{count}} balanced assignments toward {{judgesPerProject}} judges per project
assignments.random_mode_desc: Best for larger review queues. Each filtered project is filled toward {{judgesPerProject}} judges, with {{count}} new assignments planned.
assignments.bulk_mode_desc: Assign every filtered project to the {{judges}} selected judges. Best for smaller events or full re-review. {{count}} new assignments are planned.
assignments.auto_hint: Balanced random assignment is the safest default. It fills the {{count}} filtered projects toward {{judgesPerProject}} judges without removing or overwriting existing assignments.
